name: ping
summary: Tests whether a machine answers on the network.
description: Sends ICMP “echo request” packets to a host and measures the response time (time=… ms). On Linux, ping keeps going forever: Ctrl+C stops it and prints a summary (packets lost, min/average/max times). No answer does not prove the machine is off: many firewalls block ICMP.

options.description: Number of packets to send before stopping.
Interval between two packets, in seconds (1 by default).
How long to wait for each reply, in seconds.
Size of the data in each packet, in bytes.

example.output: 1408 bytes from server.local (192.168.1.20): icmp_seq=1 ttl=64 time=1.9 ms
64 bytes from 142.250.179.110: icmp_seq=1 ttl=117 time=12.4 ms
64 bytes from 2a00:1450:4007:80c::200e: icmp_seq=1 ttl=117 time=13.1 ms

options.description: Quiet mode: only the final summary.

example.output:
10 packets transmitted, 10 received, 0% packet loss, time 9013ms
rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 11.8/12.4/13.9/0.6 ms

arguments.name: HOST
arguments.description: Domain name or IP address to test.

examples.explanation: Sends 4 packets then prints the summary.
